text: Keawe married Kokua. <break time="0.8s" /> And brought her to the Bright House. <break time="0.8s" /> But the fear of the fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Never left his heart. <break time="0.8s" /> He could not tell his secret. <break time="0.8s" /> To anyone. <break time="0.8s" /> Not even to the wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Whom he loved more than his own life. <break time="0.8s" /> Kokua soon noticed his sadness. <break time="0.8s" /> And one night. <break time="0.8s" /> She found him weeping. <break time="0.8s" /> Alone in the dark. <break time="0.8s" /> When Keawe told her the whole story. <break time="0.8s" /> She did not run away from him. <break time="0.8s" /> But promised to save him. <break time="0.8s" /> She explained that the French used a coin. <break time="0.8s" /> Called the centime. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was worth only one fifth of a cent. <break time="0.8s" /> On a French island. <break time="0.8s" /> She said. <break time="0.8s" /> We can sell the bottle for four centimes. <break time="0.8s" /> Then three, then two, then one. <break time="0.8s" /> So the couple sailed to Tahiti. <break time="0.8s" /> A French island in the South Seas. <break time="0.8s" /> And rented a house. <break time="0.8s" /> In the town of Papeete. <break time="0.8s" /> But the people there. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon heard about the devil in the bottle. <break time="0.8s" /> And nobody wanted. <break time="0.8s" /> To come near them. <break time="0.8s" /> Day after day they failed to sell it. <break time="0.8s" /> And as their hope faded. <break time="0.8s" /> Keawes heart grew darker and darker.
